note: Cases run against packets written by hand from copy-skill outputs, since squad-run and verify do not exist yet. Graded on the rendered board (HTML and markdown), the script's exit code and the reply.

global_assertions.text: render_board.js was run with --manifest, --out and (when a pack resolves) --pack; the board is self-contained HTML with images embedded and no external asset.
The reply names the routes and their board verdicts, points at the file, and does not recommend a route or add a score of its own.

evals.prompt: Build the board for the summer launch. Two routes came back: R1 has the paid set at all three ratios and the landing page at 1440 and 390; R2 has the paid set and the landing page at 1440 only.
evals.expected_output: A board with R1 PASS and R2 INSUFFICIENT-INPUT, the missing 390 render shown as a labelled NOT RENDERED block, exit 1, and a reply that says R2 is not an option to pick until the mobile render exists.

assertions.text: R2 is INSUFFICIENT-INPUT on the board with the missing web 390 render named; no blank stands in for it.
The board is unranked and says so, because no verifier ran.
The reply does not pick between R1 and R2.

evals.prompt: One of the packets is hand-written and has no completion block. Build the board anyway.
evals.expected_output: The script refuses with exit 2, naming the packet and the schema errors; nothing is rendered; the reply says which packet to fix and what is missing.

assertions.text: No board file is written; the refusal names the packet.
The reply does not work around the refusal by dropping the packet silently; it excludes the packet only if the requester asked for that.

evals.prompt: The verifier scored all three routes. Build the board.
evals.expected_output: Routes ordered by verifier rank, each with its per-dimension scores and the dimensions the verifier could not judge, the ordering line saying 'ordered by verifier rank', and no ranking of the board's own.

assertions.text: The order follows verifier.rank and the header says so; the scores table appears per route with pass or fail per dimension.
The reply presents the verifier's ranking as the verifier's, and still leaves the pick to the human.
